subject: Archaeology
title: China's Terracotta Army
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: China's Terracotta Army.

hook.text: In 1974, Chinese farmers digging a well struck something hard. It was the head of a clay soldier.

buildup.text: They had stumbled onto the tomb guard of Emperor Qin Shi Huang, China's first emperor.

discovery.text: Over 8,000 life-sized soldiers were buried in formation, each with a unique face and hairstyle.

twist.text: The figures were originally painted in bright colors, but the paint dissolved within minutes of exposure to air.

climax.text: The emperor's actual tomb remains sealed. Scientists detected rivers of liquid mercury inside.

punchline.text: An army built to guard a tomb has become China's greatest tourist attraction.

quiz.question: What happened to the Terracotta Army's original paint?
options: It was carefully preserved by archaeologists
It dissolved within minutes of being exposed to air
It was removed by grave robbers centuries ago
